transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-03
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Luis Ortega (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (CTO, Sundial), Ben Smith (Eng Mgr, Sundial), Aisha Khan (Head Security, Sundial)

Summary (auto): quick renewal/retainer discussion, agreement on capacity bump for EU edge pilot, clarification on private key management/KMS, next steps to run benchmark and send SOW/pricing.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. Quick check, audio okay?
[00:05] Priya Rao: Yep, loud and clear, thanks Maya.
[00:12] Luis Ortega: Morning, all. I'll share screen in a bit, but first just want to get context — are we still on the retainer refresh path, and target start for EU edge pilot is mid-March?
[00:24] Priya Rao: Correct. We're looking to extend the retainer, bump capacity ~35% for EU traffic, and want a short pilot in eu-west that uses your dedicated edge pool. Also want to confirm data residency and KMS flow.
[00:37] Ben Smith: Also need to validate p99 latency under peak — our SLAs are tight for checkout flows.
[00:43] Maya Chen: Totally. Today's goal is to align on the scope (capacity, regions), list out security docs needed, and lock dates for the benchmark and SOW turnaround.

[01:02] Luis Ortega: Quick note — when you say "EU edge", do you mean Redwood Dedicated in eu-west with private VPC peering, or a Private deployment on-prem-ish? There's a cost and latency tradeoff.
[01:18] Priya Rao: We prefer Redwood Dedicated in eu-west with VPC peering into our cloud tenant; on-prem is likely too heavy for this phase.
[01:26] Aisha Khan: From security side, we need KMS integration details (we use AWS KMS + external HSM for key custody) and your audit log retention. Also SOC 2 type II evidence if possible.
[01:40] Maya Chen: Yep - we can provide SOC2 report and our security pack. KMS/HSM is supported — we have an HSM integration path, though there's an initial onboarding window. We'll document that.

[02:05] Luis Ortega: I'll also surface the efficient path — for the pilot we recommend trying a quantized FP16 variant plus a near-FP16 fallback. That keeps cost down and usually keeps p99 in bounds, but it's workload dependent. We'll run both.
[02:20] Ben Smith: When you say quantized, do you mean 8-bit or 4-bit? We've seen quality cliffs at lower precision for some of our prompts.
[02:28] Luis Ortega: Good call — we'll test 8-bit quant and compare to FP16. We'll run the prompt set you shared last week and also a synthetic spiky load to measure p95/p99 under burst.

[03:00] Speaker 1: (mumbling) there's a shared spreadsheet right — the cost run?
[03:05] Priya Rao: Yes, Maya you sent a pricing workbook last week.
[03:08] Maya Chen: I did — link in the follow-up email, but we'll send an updated tab with retainer adjustments and burst capacity add-on.

[04:10] Luis Ortega: Tech question — how are you routing traffic today? Is there an API gateway in front that we should be aware of, and what are average request sizes / token counts?
[04:22] Ben Smith: We run Kong and have a set of mid-tier services doing rate limiting. Average request is small (~80 tokens) but during checkout we see bursts with context ~700-800 tokens from the session state.
[04:35] Luis Ortega: That matters for KV cache sizing and memory planning. We'll size the node pools for the sequence length distribution.

[05:10] Priya Rao: Regarding contract, we prefer a 12-month retainer with an option to increase capacity at pre-agreed tiers. Can Redwood do a mid-term uplift clause?
[05:20] Maya Chen: Absolutely. We usually include amendment tiers in the SOW so you can bump to +25% or +50% without renegotiating the base rates; beyond that we do a short reprice. We'll put that language in.

[06:00] Aisha Khan: On audit logs — we need immutable logs for admin actions and key access, retained for 12 months, and an API to pull them into our SIEM. Is that available?
[06:12] Maya Chen: Yes, we have audit log exports and can push to your S3 or syslog; retention is configurable. We'll include the retention SLA in the security appendix.

[07:05] Luis Ortega: For the benchmark cadence — propose 72-hour continuous run on eu-west, with two config variants: 1) FP16 baseline; 2) 8-bit quantized. We'll capture latency histograms, error rates, and token throughput.
[07:20] Ben Smith: That sounds good. We also want to include a synthetic spike test to mimic holiday checkout-like traffic.
[07:27] Luis Ortega: Noted. We'll simulate spikes up to 3x normal traffic.

[08:00] Speaker 2: (brief crosstalk)
[08:12] Priya Rao: Pricing — we need the retainer numbers so finance can sign off. Any chance of a blended rate for the retainer months versus pilot months?
[08:22] Maya Chen: We typically give a pilot discount and then a committed monthly rate. For the retainer we can offer a small discount if you commit to the 12-month minimum and the capacity tiers. I'll send updated workbook with blended pilot pricing.

[09:00] Luis Ortega: A thing to call out — if you route to dedicated edge, there can be transient cold-starts for KV cache warming when you scale up nodes; but we've got pre-warm mechanisms and auto-prefix caching to reduce that. We'll document the expected warm-up window.
[09:22] Ben Smith: How long is that warm-up typically?
[09:25] Luis Ortega: For your workload probably 30–90s for prefix warming, but full steady-state maybe a few minutes depending on traffic. We'll show traces in the benchmark results.

[10:10] Aisha Khan: We also need to know where keys are stored in your flow — is customer key material ever present in Redwood-managed storage? We prefer customer-managed keys.
[10:22] Maya Chen: Customer-managed KMS is supported; keys remain in your KMS, Redwood only sees ciphertext. We'll include the keyflow diagram in the security pack.

[11:00] Priya Rao: SLA question — what happens if you can't meet the p99 target during a sustained period? Do you have fallback model routing or regional failover?
[11:12] Luis Ortega: Yes, we support smart routing and automatic fallback to a lower-cost compatible model or to another region if necessary. We can configure automatic rollback policies for rollouts and traffic shaping to preserve availability.

[12:05] Ben Smith: For the pilot, we want logging to capture token-level cost so we can correlate cost vs latency. Is that available?
[12:15] Maya Chen: Yes, Redwood Console has token-level cost/latency breakdowns; we'll ensure you have access to the trial Console and a dashboard for the pilot.

[12:55] Luis Ortega: Small note — sometimes Fireflies transcript swallows code names. We had an internal note calling the EU edge "Project Dune" — apologies if that appears in docs.
[13:05] Priya Rao: (laughs) noted.

[14:00] Speaker 3: (unlabeled) question about data residency, is there a compliance checkbox?
[14:05] Maya Chen: Yes — we can lock region, ensure no cross-region replication, and document data flow. We'll also provide a short attestation for EU data residency for the pilot.

[15:00] Luis Ortega: Ok, timeline recap — SOW + pricing by March 7, benchmark window March 15–17 (pilot kick-off week), results/trace share by March 21, decision on retainer uplift by March 25. Does that align?
[15:18] Priya Rao: Those dates work for us, pending legal review.

[16:00] Ben Smith: One more technical ask — can you provide estimated cost per 1M tokens for the quantized run vs fp16 on the proposed dedicated pool? Finance needs that number.
[16:12] Maya Chen: We'll add an estimated per-token run rate to the pricing sheet. It's an estimate because actual depends on batching and hit-rate on the KV cache.

[17:20] Aisha Khan: Also, can you list people for the SOC2 contact? We need an admin to ping for compliance evidence.
[17:30] Maya Chen: I'll include security contacts in the SOW attachment — primary and secondary.

[18:00] Priya Rao: Anything else — open to suggestions to reduce cost?
[18:05] Luis Ortega: For cost optimization, consider caching more session context on the client and using prefix caching on Redwood side, plus token trimming strategies. Also plan for larger batch windows during predictable low-latency periods.
[18:20] Ben Smith: We'll review prompt engineering and see where we can trim tokens.

[19:00] Speaker 1: (brief) can you also share example logging schema?
[19:05] Luis Ortega: Yes — we'll send the template for token-level logs and latency histograms.

[20:00] Maya Chen: Quick recap of next steps — I'll send SOW + pricing (Maya), Luis will run benchmark and upload results, Aisha will provide KMS/HSM details, Ben will send traffic profile. Schedule pilot for week of March 15.
[20:22] Priya Rao: Sounds good, thanks all.
[20:30] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with calendar invite for pilot kickoff and share the repo/spreadsheet.

[21:00] (meeting ends)

Notes / Links referenced: pricing workbook (link sent via email), security pack (SOC2 + KMS keyflow diagram) — attachments to be posted in follow-up.

--- End of transcript ---
